- If sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., > 0.5) and forecast is falling, increase forecast by 5–10% to avoid underestimating momentum.  
- When recent price spikes occur (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model tends to overshoot — cap forecast peak at 10–15% above recent high.  
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating +/– >0.3) and forecast is smooth, introduce 1–2% noise or slight downward bias to reflect uncertainty.  
- If forecast consistently lags true outcome by 2–3 days (especially after spikes), add 1–2% upward bias to next-day forecast to account for lagged momentum.  
- If sentiment is neutral or weak (±0.1–0.2) and forecast is trending, apply mean reversion: if forecast > 1.5σ above recent mean, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows strong downward trend after a spike, reduce forecast by 3–5% per day for next 3–5 days to reflect cooling momentum.
